text: Hello everyone, welcome to my class.Today we are going to start a new unit.This unit introduces the theme of life and cultures of different peoples across the globe.In today's class, we are going to do a comprehensive reading of the passage, making school meaningful.By the end of this lesson, you are expected to grasp the general meaning of the passage and describe the daily life and the education of the Yupik people.Also, you are supposed to explore the importance of preserving the local culture and making it a part of school education.Please get your textbook and worksheet ready.Are you ready?Here we go.Before we start reading the passage, please look at the photos and think about these three questions.Question 1.How would you describe the environment?What do you think life is like for teenagers there?What might they do in their free time?Yes, for the first question, you may think it must be very cold there.There are not many green plants around.For the second question, some students believe that life may be hard for teenagers there, and perhaps they have to help their families hunt or fish to make a living.What's more, in their free time, many teenagers might go skating or skiing with their friends.Good job, let's move on.Look at the title.What do you think the passage is about?Pay attention to the keyword school.Yes, this passage may be about the life and education of teenagers living on St.Lawrence Island.Now, I believe you all have a brief idea about the topic we are going to talk about today.Please skim the whole passage and finish the matching exercise.You will have two minutes.Thumbs up.How did you divide the passage according to your understanding?Yes, the first part is a specific case of a teenager who lives on St.Paragraph A and B are included in the first part.The second part tells the simple life of local people and the disappointing education.It includes paragraph C, D, and E.The third part states conflicts between tradition and modernization.That is paragraph F and G, while the last paragraph is about native people's expectation of education reform.Wagner, a high school student, is going to lead us to the world of Yupik people on St.Lawrence Island in Alaska.Here's a small tip.The name Wagner derives from Germanic language, so it is pronounced as Wagner.I'm sure you can't wait to know more about his life and education there.Let's get started.Now read the first part with the following two questions in your mind.What is Wagner good at?Why isn't Wagner planning to go to college?You will have 30 seconds.Have you finished?Let's check the answers together.Wagner knows a lot about biology and math.He is also good at hunting fish.He's really talented, right?Then why isn't this talented boy planning to go to college?First, he feels a responsibility for his brother and sisters, and college is so far from home.College means higher education.Literally, college is far from home in distance, while it also means that a college education is hardly relevant to his present life.Going to college seems to be a dream impossible to realize.Have you noticed the signal words also here?Here's the second reason.He's also unclear about what he would do with a degree.Notice that the use of the word would signals subjunctive mood.Even if he gets a college degree, it is unlikely for him to find a job on this remote island.So why did the writer mention Wagner?Actually, the writer starts the passage with a specific case to introduce the topic, if the education there is meaningful.Let's dig deeper and read part two.Try to answer the following question.Why do so few students from St.Lawrence Island go to college?You will have two minutesWhy do so few students from St.You will have two minutesOkay, time's up.Let's go through the question together.Here, a subsistence lifestyle means the state of having just enough money or food to stay alive.And the largest employer is the school system.There are only a handful of jobs.Here, a handful of jobs means a small amount of jobs.Let's continue reading paragraph D and E.That means the school curriculum may not teach the children how to solve problems in real life or how to make a living.The second reason is that family also worry that sending children away to study in higher education could endanger the Yupik language and culture.Their traditions, language and culture may disappear if the younger generation are educated outside of the island.So, can the community send more students to university without losing its native culture and language?Now, let's explore the third part and find more information.You might be curious about what community here refers to.Obviously, it refers to Yupik people.Then, why do they have a strong sense of community?And what are the conflicts between tradition and modernization?Now, please read part three with these two questions in your mind.Have you got the answer?As Wagner put it, we are all one big family because we are so isolated.We can see from paragraph F, there are only a small number of people living on the island.They have lived on the small island for 2,000 years and are used to the harsh environment.How do we know that?Let's take a close look at this sentence.In the summer, fields of grassy frozen ground stretch from snow-capped mountain ranges to the stony shorelines.But in the winter, the sun disappears.There is a lot of snow and polar bears arrive on ice floes.So, it is extremely cold here.They are really isolated and have to depend on each other as one big family.The sense of community is strong.From paragraph F, we can see that Yupik people are leading such a remote life with a quite small population.What changes are taking place on the island?What are the locals' attitudes towards them?Actually, their lifestyles are changing.The children drink soda and eat macaroni and cheese.Rice snow machines play video games and watch TV.Even if the changes are inevitable,the local people are making efforts to protect their independence and their heritage.Here comes the last part of this passage.What are the native people's expectations of education reform?You will have one minute to read through part
